newsitem.title: UK: Dixons down on MMC price fixing worries.
newsitem.headline: Dixons down on MMC price fixing worries.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc and Kingfisher Plc were down on Friday following a report the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) could ban recommended retail prices for a wide range of electrical goods.
"This is not good news for Dixons and Kingfisher", an analyst said, adding this would make the market freer as the retailers were not able to use its market power.
The Economist reported on Friday that the MMC was about to demand an end to the use of recommended retail prices and to require the manufacturers to promise not to seek to control prices.
"A wave of discounts could follow and sales could come down", one trader said.

By 0825 GMT, Dixons, Britain's leading electrical appliances retailer was down 10-1/2p to 464-1/2 in volume of over one million shares while Kingfisher, owner of the rival Comet chain, fell 8-1/2p to 711-1/2.
Early in May, analysts at Verdict Research said suppliers called the tune in Britain's electricals retailing market, which may work against consumers' interests.
Retailers do not operate a cartel, but there was a virtual price uniformity, Verdict Research said.
